title: Fourier expansion on $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$
statement:
Fix integers $k \ge 1$ and $n$, and let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. For a frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, let $\chi_s(x) = \omega_k^{\,s\cdot x}$ be the corresponding Fourier character, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\hat f(s) = \tfrac{1}{k^n}\sum_{x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n} f(x)\,\overline{\chi_s(x)}$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $s$. Then every function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ is recovered from its Fourier coefficients by
\[
  f(x) = \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n} \hat f(s)\,\chi_s(x)
  \qquad\text{for all } x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n.
\]
replaced:
Every function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ admits the Fourier expansion
\[
  f(x) = \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n} \hat{f}(s)\,\chi_s(x).
\]
The characters form a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(\mathbb{Z}_k^n)$.
